Proposal

Applications added, switched off and removed on a running server

proposal/live-applications2026-11-08Giovanni Porcariaccepted

Problem

The set of applications is fixed when the server is built. To intervene on a running server, for example to mount a debug application, use it and take it away, the server must be restarted.

The design of the server asks for the opposite: installing and removing an application are operations on a running machine, not reasons to restart it. The configuration is meant as a live tree that notifies whoever watches it. Neither exists in the code (kajenn-org/kajenn#75).

Current state

readsrc/kajenn/server.py:2532026-11-08
register_application is called only while the server is built. Its docstring says the set of applications is fixed at construction. No method removes an application.
readsrc/kajenn/application.py:2362026-11-08
An application accepts its owning server once; a second assignment raises RuntimeError.
readsrc/kajenn/config/handler.py:802026-11-08
ConfigurationHandler only reads the configuration tree. Nothing subscribes to it.

Proposed solution

Server and application: who does what

The server keeps the state of each application and answers for it. The application is responsible for behaving well: it talks to the server and tells it what it needs to know.

  • The server holds the state of each application, disabled or enabled, answers for a disabled one, and takes the signals the applications send.
  • The application retries what it needs (an external service, a database), says when it is ready, closes its own calls in progress when switched off, and removes itself when it gives up.

Two states: disabled and enabled

An application is either disabled or enabled. There is no error state. An application that fails removes itself, and the reason stays in the log.

What a client receives
SituationAnswer
Being mounted, not ready yet503 with Retry-After
Switched off503 without Retry-After
Being removed503 without Retry-After
Removed404
EnabledThe application answers

Mounting: disabled first, enabled on ready

  1. The application node is written into the live configuration.
  2. The server, subscribed to the applications branch, builds the application and registers it disabled.
  3. The application reaches its working state, retrying on its own if something it needs is missing, and sends ready.
  4. The server enables it. An application that gives up removes itself, with an explicit call. An on_startup that raises leaves the application disabled: the error is logged and nothing else happens.

Without an override, the base class sends ready as soon as the activation of the application ends. An application that must wait for something overrides it.

The end of activation is the return of on_startup. At boot the lifespan opens the databases of the server and starts the on_startup of every application without waiting for them, so the server serves at once: an application being mounted answers 503 with Retry-After, and _server is reachable. For a hot-added application the server runs on_startup right after registering it.

An application with spawner has its counterpart in the process of the server, a RemoteApplication. Its on_startup waits for the joined message of the child process, then returns; joined stays internal between the child and its counterpart.

The mechanism lives in AsgiServer, which has the KajennBus and _server. On a bare BaseServer the applications are enabled at once.

Every application follows this road: those added while the server runs and those declared in the recipe at boot. The boot is the same mounting, once per declared application.

Switching off and removing

  • Switching off is an operation of its own. The application becomes disabled, new requests receive 503, the calls in progress reach their end, and the instance stays registered.
  • Switching on makes the same instance enabled again, without building it again.
  • Removing first switches the application off, then takes it away when the application says it has finished. After that the mount answers 404.
  • An application is never moved to another mount. It can be switched off and on, or removed and mounted again.
  • _server is never disabled: disable and remove on _server answer 400.
  • Removing calls the hook on_remove of the application after it is disabled, and waits for it. When on_remove returns, the application has finished. on_shutdown stays for the shutdown of the server.

Every signal travels on the KajennBus

An application may run in the process of the server or in a process of its own (spawner="subprocess"). Every signal between an application and the server is therefore a KajennBus call to a route of _server, whatever process the application runs in. A call, not a send: the application receives the answer of the server, including a refusal.

The applications section of _server

Routes under /_server/applications/
RouteCalled byEffect
addadministratorWrites the node and builds the application disabled
readythe applicationEnables it
disableadministratorSwitches it off
enableadministratorSwitches it on again
removeadministrator, or the application itselfSwitches it off, waits for the application to finish, removes it
listadministratorThe applications, with their state

add receives what the application node of a recipe holds: the import path of the application class, its code, and the extra parameters handed to its constructor. What is added is always an application class.

Every route of the section requires the administrator role. The rule is applied through the route plugins, with no mechanism of its own.

Mandatory applications and capabilities

  • The application node takes the attribute mandatory. A mandatory application is one without which the server can do none of its work. When it fails, the server logs it and stays up for _server only: every other application answers 503, and the readiness probe /readyz answers not ready. The administrator intervenes through _server.
  • An application declares the capabilities it brings. While it is not enabled, those capabilities are missing. The declaration arrives with the env capabilities of the request (kajenn-org/kajenn#104), which are what reads it; list then shows them too.
  • A route requiring a missing capability answers 503, as the routing register already records. What to do about it is the logic of each application, case by case. The server takes no action on a missing capability.

FatalBootError

FatalBootError is a problem of the server as a whole, for example a database of the server that does not open. An on_startup no longer raises it: an application whose failure matters is mandatory. The option abort_on_fatal_boot_error of the server element chooses the effect: True, the default, ends the process as today; False keeps the server up for _server only.

Persistence

Persistence is designed here and implemented by kajenn-org/kajenn#118, after #112. Until then a hot change lasts until the restart.

  • Whoever calls add chooses whether the change survives a restart.
  • A persistent add is accepted only when the server is in develop and its shutdown_mode is QUITTING. Otherwise it is refused. Today only the --reload launcher sets QUITTING.
  • develop is read only from the machine defaults layer, $KAJENN_HOME/config.py. A site recipe that declares it is refused. Without develop the server is in production.
  • A persistent change is recorded as an operation, add or remove, in a file under <home>/data/ of the site. The file is not .py: the reload supervisor watches only *.py.
  • A QUITTING shutdown keeps the file and the next boot runs its operations in order after the recipe. A STOPPING shutdown discards it.
  • An operation of the file that fails at boot raises FatalBootError naming the operation: a class that does not import, a code already taken, a remove of an unknown code. The file stays.
  • An application replayed from the file whose on_startup raises stays disabled and the error is logged, as any other application.
  • --debug and --reload stay independent. In production a hot change lasts until the restart, a future soft restart included.

Decisions

decidedd-validate
When is a hot-added application checked?
  1. Before the node is written
  2. After the node is written, inside the subscription
  3. Mounted disabled, enabled when it works, removed otherwise
Choice: Mounted disabled, enabled when it works, removed otherwise (GP, 2026-11-08)
The application is built and registered disabled; it is enabled once it is in working state, and removed otherwise.
decidedd-answers
What does a client receive from an application that is not enabled?
  1. 503, with Retry-After only while it is being mounted; 404 once removed
  2. 404 in every case
Choice: 503, with Retry-After only while it is being mounted; 404 once removed (GP, 2026-11-08)
A client tells an application on its way in from one on its way out, and both from one that is gone.
decidedd-ready-who
Which applications send ready?
  1. Every application, hot-added or declared at boot
  2. Only those that declare they need it
Choice: Every application, hot-added or declared at boot (GP, 2026-11-08)
One rule for every application; the boot is the same mounting.
decidedd-signal-road
How does an application signal the server?
  1. A Python call on the server
  2. A KajennBus call to a route of _server
Choice: A KajennBus call to a route of _server (GP, 2026-11-08)
An application can run in a process of its own; everything goes through the KajennBus.
decidedd-retry
Who retries when something an application needs is missing?
  1. The application
  2. The server, through a readiness check of the application
Choice: The application (GP, 2026-11-08)
The server only waits for the signal.
decidedd-give-up
What does an application do when it stops retrying?
  1. It removes itself
  2. It goes into an error state and stays registered
Choice: It removes itself (GP, 2026-11-08)
No error state is kept; the reason stays in the log.
decidedd-startup-raise
What happens to an application whose on_startup raises?
  1. It removes itself, as an application giving up
  2. It stays disabled; giving up is an explicit call of the application
Choice: It stays disabled; giving up is an explicit call of the application (GP, 2026-11-10)
The exception is logged; an application that stops retrying says so itself.
decidedd-mandatory
What marks an application whose failure matters?
  1. The attribute mandatory on the application node, alongside the capabilities
  2. Only the capabilities other applications require
Choice: The attribute mandatory on the application node, alongside the capabilities (GP, 2026-11-08)
The administrator can mark an application mandatory even when no other application needs it.
decidedd-mandatory-fails
What does the server do when a mandatory application fails?
  1. It stops
  2. It stays up
  3. It stays up for _server only: the public part answers 503 and the server reports not ready
Choice: It stays up for _server only: the public part answers 503 and the server reports not ready (GP, 2026-11-09)
Without a mandatory application the server can do none of its work; it stays alive only so that _server can answer. Refines the choice of 2026-11-08, It stays up.
decidedd-capabilities
Who acts when a capability is missing?
  1. The server, by not enabling the applications that need it
  2. Nobody: the routes requiring it are unavailable, and each application decides
Choice: Nobody: the routes requiring it are unavailable, and each application decides (GP, 2026-11-08)
Its routes are simply not available; the logic of the application decides case by case.
decidedd-switch-off
Is switching off an operation of its own?
  1. Yes, and it is the first step of removing
  2. No: switching off means removing
Choice: Yes, and it is the first step of removing (GP, 2026-11-08)
Removing passes through switching off, which lets the calls end and blocks new ones.
decidedd-server-self
Can _server be switched off or removed?
  1. No: disable and remove on _server answer 400
  2. Yes
Choice: No: disable and remove on _server answer 400 (GP, 2026-11-09)
_server is the door the administrator intervenes from.
decidedd-remove-hook
How does the server ask an application to finish before removing it?
  1. on_shutdown
  2. A hook of its own, on_remove, called after the application is disabled
Choice: A hook of its own, on_remove, called after the application is disabled (GP, 2026-11-09)
on_shutdown stays for the shutdown of the server. Lifecycle hooks are named on_<verb> when they run before the event completes and on_<verb>_done when they run after.
decidedd-activation
What is the end of activation, after which the base class sends ready?
  1. The return of on_startup
  2. A new hook
Choice: The return of on_startup (GP, 2026-11-09)
Simpler to use on_startup.
decidedd-boot-detached
At boot, does the lifespan wait for the on_startup of the applications?
  1. Yes, as today: nothing is served until they all return
  2. No: the server serves at once, applications being mounted answer 503
Choice: No: the server serves at once, applications being mounted answer 503 (GP, 2026-11-09)
decidedd-joined
How does an application in a separate process become ready?
  1. Its process calls ready, and joined disappears
  2. The on_startup of its RemoteApplication waits for joined, then the base class sends ready
Choice: The on_startup of its RemoteApplication waits for joined, then the base class sends ready (GP, 2026-11-09)
The counterpart in the server process sends ready when it knows its child is ready.
decidedd-bare-server
How do the applications of a bare BaseServer, with no KajennBus and no _server, become enabled?
  1. They are enabled at once
  2. The KajennBus and _server move into BaseServer
Choice: They are enabled at once (GP, 2026-11-09)
The mechanism lives in AsgiServer, the server of every real site.
decidedd-fatal
What is FatalBootError once the lifespan no longer waits for on_startup?
  1. A problem of the server as a whole; its effect is chosen by abort_on_fatal_boot_error, default True
  2. Removed in favour of mandatory
Choice: A problem of the server as a whole; its effect is chosen by abort_on_fatal_boot_error, default True (GP, 2026-11-09)
FatalBootError concerns the server, mandatory concerns one application. Default delegated: True, the behaviour of today.
decidedd-move
Can an application be moved to another mount?
  1. No
  2. Yes, as an operation of its own
Choice: No (GP, 2026-11-08)
It can be switched off and on, not moved.
decidedd-persist
Does a hot change survive a restart?
  1. Whoever adds the application decides
  2. Never
  3. Always
Choice: Whoever adds the application decides (GP, 2026-11-08)
The persistent case needs an extra configuration file with the updates; it is designed later.
decidedd-persist-when
On which servers may a hot change be persistent?
  1. Only in develop and with a soft shutdown (QUITTING)
  2. Only with --debug
  3. On every server
Choice: Only in develop and with a soft shutdown (QUITTING) (GP, 2026-11-10)
The development cycle must not lose a hot change at each reload. In production the configuration is not persistent, for security.
decidedd-persist-develop
How does the server know it runs on a developer machine?
  1. A develop flag in the machine defaults layer, read only there
  2. A production flag on the production hosts
  3. --debug
  4. The presence of a reverse proxy
Choice: A develop flag in the machine defaults layer, read only there (GP, 2026-11-10)
A missing file then removes persistence instead of opening it. A site recipe cannot change what the machine allows.
decidedd-persist-file
What does the extra file hold, and where?
  1. The operations made after the start, in the data folder of the site
  2. The final state of the added and removed applications
  3. A file per site in $KAJENN_HOME
Choice: The operations made after the start, in the data folder of the site (GP, 2026-11-10)
Only the changes after the start. The file follows the folder of the site.
decidedd-persist-replay
What happens when an operation of the file fails at boot?
  1. The boot stops with FatalBootError
  2. The operation is skipped with a warning
  3. The whole file is discarded with a warning
Choice: The boot stops with FatalBootError (GP, 2026-11-10)
Simpler: nothing already run has to be undone.
decidedd-routes
Which routes does _server expose?
  1. Section applications: add, ready, disable, enable, remove, list
Choice: Section applications: add, ready, disable, enable, remove, list (GP, 2026-11-08)
One section for the whole life of an application.
decidedd-auth
Who may call the routes of the applications section?
  1. One rule: the administrator role on every route
  2. Two rules: an application may call ready and remove on its own code
Choice: One rule: the administrator role on every route (GP, 2026-11-08)
One rule for now, applied through the route plugins.
decidedd-add-payload
What does add receive?
  1. The class path, the code and the extra parameters, as the application node of a recipe
Choice: The class path, the code and the extra parameters, as the application node of a recipe (GP, 2026-11-08)
It says what, under which name and with which extra parameters; what is always an application class.
decidedd-ready-base
Does the base class send ready at the end of the startup of an application that adds nothing?
  1. Yes: an application overrides it only when it needs more
  2. No: every application writes its own call
Choice: Yes: an application overrides it only when it needs more (GP, 2026-11-08)
Without an override the application sends ready as soon as its activation ends.

Consequences

  • The set of applications is no longer fixed at construction. The server gains a road to remove an application.
  • The server subscribes to the applications branch of the live configuration. It is the first subscriber of that tree.
  • Every application, at boot too, answers 503 until it sends ready.
  • The design of the server stops listing the move of an application to another prefix among the operations on a running server.
